NovaPharm Biotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaPharm Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and limiting to one question will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaPharm Biotech's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Ellis, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Marcus Lee, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial; and Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, CEO of NovaPharm Biotech.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. NovaPharm Biotech delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand across our oncology and cardio-metabolic franchises, significant pipeline advancements, and disciplined execution amid a competitive landscape. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, positioning us as a leader in next-generation therapies.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, including our strategic priorities and outlook, overall performance highlights and key takeaways, revenue guidance and key upcoming catalysts, product revenue by key franchises, clinical trial updates, geographic revenue breakdown, and R&D investments. We are particularly excited about NP-401, our next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, and its potential to transform frontline NSCLC treatment with superior efficacy.

To kick things off, let me highlight a few top-line points before turning to our executives for deeper dives. Our Q3 results reflect exceptional execution, with total revenue of $2.85 billion, up 28% year-over-year, beating expectations and marking our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth. This was powered by standout performances from NovoLir in obesity and diabetes, OncoTarget in oncology, and steady contributions from our legacy assets. Pipeline-wise, we hit key milestones like positive Phase 3 toplines for NP-401 and interim data from NP-567's cardio-vision trial.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Ellis, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Ellis, CFO:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 35% volume growth in our commercial products like NovoLir and OncoTarget, milestone payments from partners such as Regeneron, and collaboration revenue from our gene therapy JVs.

Let me walk you through our overall performance highlights and key takeaways for the third quarter, which underscore another period of exceptional execution across our portfolio. We delivered robust top-line growth, expanded margins, and meaningful pipeline momentum, all while navigating a dynamic macroeconomic and regulatory environment in biotech and pharma.

Starting with the headline numbers: Q3 total revenue came in at $2.85 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, handily beating our guidance midpoint and consensus expectations by $150 million. Commercial product sales, which now represent 72% of total revenue, surged 35% YoY to $2.05 billion. NovoLir alone generated $1.4 billion in net sales, a staggering 52% YoY increase, fueled by expanded label indications for cardiovascular risk reduction—approved by the FDA in June—and peak-season demand ahead of the holiday weight management push. Sequential volume growth was 12%, with average realized pricing holding steady despite payer pushback. Our next-gen oncology asset, OncoTarget—a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody—ramped to $450 million in sales, up 40% YoY, as it gains traction in frontline NSCLC, eroding share from Merck's Keytruda. Legacy products contributed $150 million, flat YoY but with improved gross margins from manufacturing efficiencies.

Royalty and milestone revenue added $500 million, highlighted by a $200 million upfront from Regeneron on positive Phase 2b data for our shared IL-33 inhibitor in atopic dermatitis. Collaboration revenue from our gene therapy joint venture chipped in another $150 million tied to milestones.

On the bottom line, GAAP net income was $850 million, or $1.62 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $1.12 billion, or $2.15 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.1 billion, reflecting 12% YoY growth, with R&D at 22% of revenue—down from 25% last year—due to disciplined spend on high-ROI programs. We ended the quarter with $4.8 billion in cash, providing dry powder for M&A.

Turning to product revenue performance by key drug franchise, with volume and price analysis—these figures represent net product sales after deductions, sourced from IQVIA and internal data. Total net product sales for Q3 were $2.85 billion, up 14% YoY and 6% Q/Q, driven by volume in oncology and immunology, offset by U.S. pricing headwinds from PBMs and IRA impacts.

Oncology franchise: $1.42 billion, +22% YoY. NovaLizumab, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific, delivered $1.18 billion, up 25% YoY. Volume +18% YoY, with 12% TRx growth to 285,000 prescriptions and 28% NRx share in NSCLC; ASP flat at $142,000 per patient-year. NovaTarg-3 contributed $240 million, up 45% on 30% volume and 10% ASP uplift.

Immunology: $890 million, +8% YoY. ImmunoBlock posted $720 million, +6% YoY; volume +12%, ASP -4% to $38,500. Blockade-X added $170 million.

Rare diseases: $540 million, +5% YoY. GeneFix $320 million, volume +15%, ASP -3% to $2.8 million.

Volume drove 75% of growth, U.S. 65% of sales.

Geographically, U.S. 60% or $1.71 billion, up 10% YoY from OncoVance and MetaSlim. Europe 20% or $570 million, flat YoY on pricing but +8% volume. Rest of World 20% or $570 million, up 18%; emerging markets $420 million, +25% YoY—China +35%, India +28%, LATAM +22%—via partnerships like WuXi and Dr. Reddy's, localized manufacturing, and tenders.

Now, on R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities: In Q3, GAAP R&D was $1.42 billion, up 18% YoY, or 28% of revenue. Cumulative H1 spend $2.78 billion, toward FY guidance $5.6-5.9 billion. Allocated: oncology 45%, immunology 25%, rare diseases 20%. Trends include precision oncology with companion diagnostics, IL-23 inhibitors, CRISPR hemophilia. Platforms: AI drug discovery with Insilico, continuous bioprocessing in Singapore reducing costs 25%. U.S. 55% spend, Asia-Pacific 20%.

As we wrap up a transformative Q3, let me dive into our strategic priorities and full-year outlook. Our North Star is sustainable high-teens revenue growth via ADCs, bispecifics, CRISPR. R&D at 28% of revenue, $1.2 billion this year.

Priority 1: Pipeline acceleration—NP-401 Phase 3 topline 42% PFS risk reduction vs. Keytruda, BLA Q1 2025, $4.5B peak. NP-567 22% weight loss, file YE24, $100B obesity market. CRISPR Phase 2 sickle cell H1 2025.

Priority 2: Commercial excellence—NovaLung +32% to $450M. U.S. 65%, Europe 22%, Asia 10% growth via Shanghai JV.

Priority 3: M&A—$2.5B deployed, e.g., Aura retinal assets; $800M for ADCs.

Financial outlook: FY2024 revenue $10.9-11.1B (24-27% growth), adj EPS $8.40-8.60. Q4 $1.15-1.2B. 2025 $5.6-5.9B? Wait, aligning: FY24 $10.9-11.1B, 2025 22-25% growth. Gross margins 82%.

Before Q&A, forward-looking update on revenue guidance and catalysts. Raising FY24 to $10.9-11.1B, 26-34% growth midpoint. Product sales $2.85-3.0B? Q3 context. Q4 $850-950M. Catalysts: Q3 PDUFA AETH-202 expansion, Q4 Phase 3 AETH-301 prostate, H1 2025 gene BLA.

Our cash position remains strong at $4.8 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $10.9-11.1 billion, adjusted EPS $8.40-8.60.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Emily Chen, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Before diving into financials earlier, Johnathan touched on this, but let me expand on key clinical trial updates: phase progression, data readouts, regulatory milestones across lead programs like NBX-101 ADC, NBX-202 bispecific, NBX-303 gene therapy.

For NBX-101 in HER2-low breast/gastric: Completed Phase 2b enrollment 312 patients, interim ASCO ORR 68%, DoR 14.2 months, PFS HR 0.42. Phase 3 NOVEL-3 first patient in, 75% enrollment YE24, topline Q3 2026. FDA BTD/SPA, EMA PIP. Peak $2.5B.

NBX-202 CD19xCD3: Phase 1/2 LUMIN-1 CR 72%, persistence 85%. Phase 3 LUMIN-2 first in July, 50% Q1 2025. ODD/PRV. Asia via BeiGene.

NBX-303 Pompe: Phase 1/2 47% 6MWD increase, low immunogenicity. Phase 3 IND Q4 2024, EMA PRIME. $800M peak.

Pipeline success 45%, AI stratification. We expect to file multiple BLAs in 2025.

Next, Dr. Marcus Lee will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Marcus Lee, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Emily. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Building on clinical momentum, our research includes AI-accelerated ADC discovery identifying 17 novel candidates, CRISPR-Cas9 with 95% efficiency, continuous bioprocessing at 120,000L, mRNA oncology vaccines. Platforms like AlphaFold protein engineering, PROTAC-ADCs for AACR 2025. We're advancing precision medicine, gene editing JVs, hedging supply disruptions.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Marcus. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with 35% YoY growth in key products. NovoLir captured share in $50B obesity market via CVS formulary, Medicare coverage. OncoTarget 42% TRx in HER2. Marketing campaigns effective in NRx gains, patient programs covering 95%, value-based pricing. Ex-U.S. ramps in Europe/Asia via PRIME, NMPA. Biosimilars mitigated by 505(b)(2).

Finally, Tom Reilly will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Singapore biologics at 120,000L, 22% COGS reduction via continuous processing. Ireland fill-finish scaled for mRNA/ADCs. Backward integration North Carolina APIs, dual-sourcing linkers. Shanghai JV 50M doses NP-567 by 2027. Focused on localization EM, 15% COGS savings AI-driven, resilience post-COVID disruptions. Key priorities: 20% capacity expansion, inflation hedge 5-7%.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Tom. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the Q&A session. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On NP-401, can you elaborate on the Phase 3 data versus Keytruda and BLA timeline risks?

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thanks, Mike. The 42% PFS risk reduction and 68% ORR in NSCLC frontline is compelling, with BLA Q1 2025 on track per FDA alignment. Risks like scrutiny on accelerated approvals mitigated by our clean profile and SPA.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee, JPMorgan:
Great results. On guidance raise to $10.9-11.1B, how much from milestones versus core sales, and 2025 outlook?

Sarah Ellis, CFO:
Sarah, thanks. About 20% from milestones like Regeneron, core products driving rest. 2025 22-25% growth to $13.3-13.9B implied, NP-401 ramp, obesity entry key.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim, Morgan Stanley:
On clinical front, details on NBX-303 Pompe data and Phase 3?

Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
David, the 47% 6MWD, 32% GSQ improvement, low antibodies position it over ERTs. Phase 3 vs. Nexviazyme IND Q4, PRIME aiding approval.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel, Barclays:
Manufacturing scale for NP-567 obesity launch—supply risks?

Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial:
Rachel, Shanghai JV ramps to 50M doses, Singapore efficiencies ensure supply amid incumbent constraints. Marketing ready for 2026 launch.

Operator:
Our next question from follow-up, Mike Johnson, Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson, Goldman Sachs:
Quick follow on EM growth—China specifics?

Sarah Ellis, CFO:
Mike, China $168M +35%, NRDL for OncoVance, WuXi localization key to tariff resilience.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaPharm Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
